sophie (perf): Heads up — after yesterday's kernel-selector rollout I'm seeing a consistent 2-2.5x tail latency increase on Llama-2-70B-ish configs for long-chat workloads. :eyes:

sophie (perf): Flamegraphs point at a hotspot in the KV cache path — lots of memcpy/fallbacks around the FP8-backed cache. Repro on dedicated staging with steady 50 tps and average seq_len 1024.

sophie (perf): Quick profiling snippet (from perf collector):
```
KV cache read:  38.7%  memcpy_kv_cache()
FP8->FP16 dequant: 14.2%  dequantize_kv_fp8_to_fp16()
Kernel select:  9.1%  choose_attention_kernel()  (prefers fused-kv path)
Runtime scheduler wait: 8.3%  (batcher stalls)
```

mike (mlinfra): ugh. That dequant step shouldn't be dominant. Did the selector start preferring the fused-kv kernel that assumes FP16 cache layout? Could be forcing an expensive conversion when cache hits would have been cheap.

anna (runtime): I rolled the selector to prefer `fused-attn-kv-v2` to reduce per-token kernel dispatch. It had microbench wins on short seqs. But we didn't fully test long-prefix workloads with FP8 quantized KV.

kai (eng): Are these sessions hitting prefix-cache eviction heuristics? If eviction churn increases, we might be writing+dequantizing more often. Any signs of higher eviction rate?

sophie (perf): Yes — eviction_rate jumped from ~0.02 to ~0.12 in that job. Most evictions happen at the 512->1024 boundary during turn-taking. suspect batching heuristics cause fragmented batches so prefix KV can't be reused effectively.

mike (mlinfra): Two hypotheses: 1) kernel selector picks fused path which is incompatible with our FP8 compressed cache layout -> runtime forces dequant on every cache access; 2) batcher split logic created many small heterogeneous batches causing cache alias misses.

anna (runtime): I can push a temporary guard in kernel selector: if KV cache is flagged as `fp8_compressed` prefer compatible kernel or fallback to pure fp16-attn kernel that reads cache without dequant. Want to try that in staging.

sophie (perf): Please do. Also can we add counters: `kv_dequant_per_hit` and `kv_memcpy_bytes` so we can quantify extra work? Right now perf traces are a bit noisy.

mike (mlinfra): Agree on counters. I'll add them and a histogram for batch-size distribution per worker. Also capture `batcher_split_reason` tags.

kai (eng): For short term rollback, we can pin kernel-selector to previous hash for Dedicated pools. If deploy-bot can do a revert that'd be safest while we triage.

deploy-bot: scheduled revert of `kernel-selector` to `@v1.8.3` on pools: staging-dedicated-1, staging-dedicated-2 at 1772345900. Revert will run canary then 100%.

sophie (perf): After revert latency dropped back to baseline in quick check. Thanks. But we still need a robust solution for FP8 KV caches — can't keep avoiding fused kernels forever.

anna (runtime): Plan: (1) add kernel-selection guard that checks cache metadata (fp8 vs fp16) and sequence-length profile before choosing fused-kv; (2) add a KV-cache shim that can expose a thin view for kernels that expect fp16 without doing a full dequant per read (lazy dequant + page-level markers); (3) tune batcher heuristics to avoid splitting by prefix length where possible.

mike (mlinfra): On point (2) — we already have page-aligned block maps for the KV store. We can mark blocks as `lazy_dequant_pending` and only materialize when kernel actually modifies the KV (writes). For reads we can provide a tiny adapter that returns an iterator which triggers dequant only for touched ranges. That should drop dequant CPU by ~70% in theory.

sophie (perf): Nice. Also let's evaluate alternate eviction policy: currently LRU-per-seq causes hot prefixes to be evicted when batches include many different seq lengths. Maybe a frequency-biased windowed-LRU or segtree that pins top-N prefixes per worker.

kai (eng): Another lever: batcher should consider `kv_compatibility_key` when grouping. If we group by (model, kv_layout, rope_scale_bucket) we reduce heterogeneity. Cost is more headroom fragmentation but should help throughput for these long-chat jobs.

anna (runtime): I'll prototype kv_layout tagging in routing metadata so batcher can see it cheaply. Also will emit `rope_scale_bucket` based on effective RoPE exponent range; some of the Llama-2 variants use nonstandard RoPE scaling that changes attention kernel choice.

mike (mlinfra): Good call. RoPE scaling impacts whether we can use rotary-fused kernels — mismatches cause us to fallback to generic attention which is slower and often expects different kv dims alignment. Add `rope_scale` into kernel capability table too.

sophie (perf): For experiments — let's run a 24h A/B: baseline (pinned selector) vs guarded selector + lazy-dequant + batcher-grouping. Key metrics: p95/p99 latency, token-CPU, kv_dequant_per_hit, eviction_rate, batch_size_hist.

anna (runtime): I'll open a short PR with the guard and instrumentation today, link here once ready.

mike (mlinfra): I'll add the histograms and a Grafana dashboard panel for the new counters. Also will push a microbenchmark that simulates prefix-heavy chat workload: `tools/sim_bench --model=llama-2-70b --seqs=1000 --alpha-prefix=0.7 --kv_layout=fp8-compressed`.

sophie (perf): Perfect. After we have numbers we can decide whether to re-enable fused-kv by default, or require an explicit `kv_layout=fp16_readable` flag during model onboarding.

kai (eng): One more: document known incompatibilities between quantized-KV formats and kernel families in infra runbook so SREs can interpret incidents faster.

sophie (perf): Agreed. Thanks team — nothing blocking for now (revert is in place). We'll reconvene after the A/B completes or earlier if instrumentation shows regressions. :thumbsup: 

anna (runtime): PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2547 (draft) — adds selector guard + kv metadata read path.

mike (mlinfra): Dashboard panel link: https://grafana.redwood.net/d/kv-cache/kv-dequant (will share final link once live).

deploy-bot: revert completed on 100% of targeted pools at 1772345912.

sophie (perf): Verified revert impact at 1772345920: p99 back to baseline on staging. We'll keep monitoring.

kai (eng): Great work. Followups: PR review, A/B schedule, infra runbook update.
